scenes.text: Imagine sitting at a royal banquet with the Emperor of France, Napoleon the Third, and realizing you’ve been given solid gold cutlery.
Back in the eighteen-fifties, aluminum was the most precious metal on Earth, costing far more than gold and silver combined.
Napoleon kept the rare aluminum utensils for his most important guests, while the lesser nobles had to settle for basic gold plates.
Since a sudden chemistry breakthrough made aluminum cheaper than dirt, what is something we value today that might become worthless tomorrow, and make sure to follow for more!
